primary_source: TMICC 2025 Annual Report (146292742.pdf) — 'Our strategy' and remuneration sections

headline_commitments.label: Growth
headline_commitments.commitment: Grow Organic Sales on average by 3% to 5% from 2026, in the medium term
headline_commitments.quote: We are positioning TMICC to grow Organic Sales on average by 3% to 5% from 2026, with an average annual Adjusted EBITDA margin improvement of 40 to 60 basis points in the medium term.
headline_commitments.attributed_to: CEO Peter ter Kulve, framed as establishing TMICC as a 'hard currency compounder'

headline_commitments.label: Margin
headline_commitments.commitment: Average annual Adjusted EBITDA margin improvement of 40 to 60 basis points, medium term
headline_commitments.note: Explicitly stated to not apply to any individual year — it's a medium-term average, so a single soft year doesn't necessarily break the commitment

headline_commitments.label: Cost / Separation Savings
headline_commitments.sub_target: 350 to 380 million of that in run-rate savings specifically from the Supply Chain Transformation pillar
headline_commitments.quote: In 2024, we launched a productivity programme targeting 500 million savings in the medium term. A key pillar of the productivity programme is Supply Chain transformation that is designed to create a lean, agile, and customer-focused network and deliver 350 to 380 million in run-rate savings.
headline_commitments.governance: A Transformation Steering Committee was established with clear accountability to drive delivery
headline_commitments.named_risk: Workforce adaptation through new structures, skill upgrades and effective change management — failure to manage this could result in cost overruns and operational disruption

headline_commitments.label: Capital Allocation
headline_commitments.commitment: Dividend payout ratio target of 40% to 60%
headline_commitments.note: The Board has established a balanced capital allocation framework designed to deliver consistent returns while funding organic growth

incentive_alignment.note: These aren't just stated ambitions — they're the literal formula behind executive bonus payouts, which is a real, structural signal that they're taken seriously internally.
incentive_alignment.gap: The exact named list making up the 'Strategic Priorities Performance Multiplier' itself wasn't found in this pass — only that it exists, applies to both the CEO and CFO, and has a defined scoring range

long_term_incentive_plan.name: Performance Share Plan (PSP)
long_term_incentive_plan.note: A second, separate incentive layer on top of the annual bonus above — multi-year share awards, evenly weighted across the same four metrics rather than skewed toward any one
long_term_incentive_plan.legacy_reference_found: A separate, differently-weighted set (30% Underlying Sales Growth / 30% Underlying Operating Profit growth / 30% Cash contribution) also appears in the same section of the report, most likely shown as a comparison to the prior Unilever-era LTIP structure rather than TMICC's current one — flagged as uncertain rather than stated as fact, since the surrounding context needed to confirm which plan it belongs to was lost in extraction

group_strategy_pillars.note: TMICC's own 3-part framework, stated at Group level and then repeated with region-specific tactics below
growth: Drive distribution and penetration in low per-capita-consumption countries (Pakistan named specifically)
Build an attractive portfolio at core snacking and refreshment 'coinage' price points
Further premiumise the portfolio in both indulgence and wellness
Build ice cream occasions with TMICC's demand generation model
productivity: Optimise supply chain end-to-end to improve capacity utilisation, service, and cost
Lead through digitalisation, automation and new technologies
reinvestment: De-bottleneck capacity and invest in quality and safety

growth: Double down on the fastest-growing (+5%) single-serve ice cream segment
Expand the portfolio of calorie-control and high-protein offerings
Rebuild the business in club, dollar store, and Away-from-Home channels
Pivot towards a digitally-led demand creation model
productivity: Latin America direct sales distribution system revamp

growth: Grow the ice cream category through innovation and retail partnerships
Move to a digitally-led demand creation model
productivity: Volume growth for higher asset utilisation

cross_cutting_initiatives.why_it_stands_out: Named as a distinct initiative in three separate places (Group, Americas, Europe) — a genuine cross-regional priority, not a one-off regional idea
cross_cutting_initiatives.partner_angle: Marketing technology, demand-generation platforms, data & analytics — TMICC is explicitly moving away from a traditional demand model toward a digital one across its whole footprint

cross_cutting_initiatives.why_it_stands_out: Directly connects to a real disclosed risk factor already in the ecosystem doc: the 3-million-unit freezer cabinet fleet is TMICC's single largest emissions category, and isn't even owned by TMICC (placed in retail outlets). Digitalising and expanding this fleet is a named priority in every region.
cross_cutting_initiatives.partner_angle: IoT/smart-cabinet technology, real-time inventory tracking, predictive replenishment, energy-efficiency retrofits

cross_cutting_initiatives.why_it_stands_out: Named specifically, not folded into generic 'productivity' language — a real, targeted program in TMICC's largest single market
cross_cutting_initiatives.partner_angle: Supply chain consulting, logistics/network optimisation technology

cross_cutting_initiatives.initiative: Latin America direct sales distribution system revamp
cross_cutting_initiatives.why_it_stands_out: A named, specific distribution-system overhaul distinct from the US supply chain reset — two separate Americas-region productivity initiatives, not one
cross_cutting_initiatives.partner_angle: Route-to-market technology, distribution/DSD (direct store delivery) systems, sales-force enablement

cross_cutting_initiatives.why_it_stands_out: Both are named explicitly as underperforming markets requiring a distinct turnaround plan, not just routine optimisation — matches the Italy 'below par, resetting the business' language already found in the FY2025 results commentary
